# ExaMLOps

> ExaMLOps is an open-source (Apache-2.0) MLOps platform for HPC systems and supercomputers. It trains machine-learning models as Slurm or Flux jobs, versions them in an MLflow registry, promotes them to production through metric and approval gates, serves them with Ray Serve, and monitors drift, cost, carbon and quality — driven by the `exa` CLI, a React + FastAPI dashboard, or an AI agent over MCP.

Key facts:

- Built for ML engineers, platform engineers and HPC operators who run models on batch-scheduled clusters, originally for the EuroHPC SEANERGYS project.
- Schedulers: Slurm, Flux, and a `mock` scheduler so everything runs on a laptop without a cluster (`EXAMLOPS_HPC_SCHEDULER=mock|slurm|flux`).
- Lifecycle: auto-discovery training pipelines (Prefect) → MLflow registry with Staging/Canary/Production aliases → gated promotion (`exa pipeline promote --if-rmse-lt …`) → Ray Serve multi-model serving with traffic splitting → drift detection and optional closed-loop retraining.
- Governance: an approval queue for CI model changes, policy-as-code, a hash-chained audit trail, RBAC and multi-tenancy, supply-chain signing, EU AI Act risk classification.
- LLMOps: versioned prompt registry, OpenAI-compatible gateway, RAG with citations, vector store, guardrails, calibrated LLM-judge evaluation.
- Agent access: `exa mcp serve` exposes the platform over the Model Context Protocol (read-only unless `--allow-writes`); the built-in Skipper agent confirms every write.
- Extensible without forking: use-case packs (`EXAMLOPS_USECASE_DIR`), provider plugins (`exa.providers.<domain>` entry points), `exa` CLI plugins (`examlops.cli_plugins`).
- Differs from Kubeflow (Kubernetes-first) by targeting HPC batch schedulers first; differs from a plain MLflow server by using MLflow as its registry and adding orchestration, gated serving, monitoring and governance around it.

- [FAQ](https://mskazemi.com/ExaMLOps/faq/): what it is, who it is for, schedulers, comparison with Kubeflow and MLflow, licensing
- [Compared with alternatives](https://mskazemi.com/ExaMLOps/compare/): ExaMLOps vs Kubeflow, MLflow alone, Ray on Slurm, ClearML and Metaflow for HPC — with sources and when to choose something else

- [Architecture](https://mskazemi.com/ExaMLOps/guides/architecture/): components and design

- [Follow a prediction](https://mskazemi.com/ExaMLOps/explore/prediction/): an inference request end to end
